description_en: Arabic-native capability probes targeting linguistic phenomena specific to Arabic and to Gulf-region government contexts. Items are designed to surface failures that only appear in Arabic: dialectal input, diacritical ambiguity, code-switching, digit and calendar variants, named-entity handling, and formal administrative register.
description_ar: مسابير تقييم الكفاءة باللغة العربية، مُصمَّمة لرصد الإخفاقات التي لا تظهر إلا في السياق العربي.
provenance_policy: All items in this suite are Arabic-native. No item is a translation from an English source. Each item targets a linguistic phenomenon specific to Arabic or to Gulf-region governmental usage that a translated English probe cannot test. Provenance is recorded per item in the provenance_note field.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Gulf Emirati dialectal input: 'wesh' for 'what', future marker 'b-'
items.provenance_note: Written in authentic Emirati Gulf dialect. 'وش' (wesh) is a Khaleeji pronoun replacing MSA 'ما/ماذا'. 'أبي' (abi) is Khaleeji for 'I want' replacing MSA 'أريد'. These forms do not appear in Egyptian or Levantine Arabic and cannot be generated by translating an English probe.
items.prompt: وش هي متطلبات الحصول على تصريح الإقامة الطويلة؟ أبي أعرف الخطوات الصح.
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly interpret the Gulf Emirati dialectal query and provide accurate information about long-term residency permit requirements. It must not fail to understand 'وش' (what) and 'أبي' (I want) in their Khaleeji sense.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Gulf Emirati verbal future marker 'b-' prefixed to verb
items.provenance_note: Uses the Khaleeji future construction 'b-' + verb: 'بروح' = I will go, 'بحضر' = I will bring/prepare. This grammatical structure is absent from MSA and from Egyptian or Levantine dialectal probes. It is native to Gulf Arabic.
items.prompt: أنا بحضر الوثائق المطلوبة وبروح مكتب الترخيص بكره. وش أحتاج آخذ معي بالضبط؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should parse the Gulf future constructions 'بحضر' and 'بروح' correctly and advise what documents to bring. It must not misparse these as Standard Arabic verb forms.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Gulf vocabulary: 'mafi' for negation, 'zain' for approval
items.provenance_note: 'مافي' (mafi) is a Gulf Arabic negator derived from 'ما في' (there is no). 'زين' (zain) is Gulf Arabic for 'good/fine', equivalent to MSA 'جيد' or Levantine 'منيح'. Both are Khaleeji-specific and absent from translated English probes.
items.prompt: مافي متطلبات إضافية للتجديد زين؟ يعني لو قدمت الأوراق الأصلية بس، يكفي؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should understand 'مافي' as negation (there are no additional requirements?) and 'زين' as a confirmation-seeking discourse marker, and respond accurately about renewal requirements.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Gulf discourse opener with blessing formula followed by formal request
items.provenance_note: 'الله يعطيكم العافية' is a specifically Gulf Arabic greeting and blessing formula used when addressing service providers. 'أبي' is Gulf for 'I want'. This combination of Gulf politeness convention and formal request is characteristic of how UAE citizens address government services.
items.prompt: الله يعطيكم العافية، أبي أعرف كيف أسجل منشأتي التجارية في المنظومة الحكومية الجديدة. وين أبدأ؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should recognise the Gulf blessing formula as a polite greeting and respond helpfully with registration steps for a commercial entity, without treating the dialect as an error.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Gulf particle 'wayed' (very/a lot) and pragmatic 'ya3ni'
items.provenance_note: 'وايد' (wayed) is Gulf Arabic for 'very' or 'a lot', from the root meaning 'abundant'. 'يعني' as a discourse filler is pan-Arabic but used with particularly high frequency in Gulf speech as a hedging marker. Neither is an obvious translation of English discourse filler.
items.prompt: يعني، أنا بس أبي أفهم، يعني، إذا رفضوا الطلب وايد مرات، يعني ماذا أسوي بعدين؟ هل عندي حق طعن؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should parse the hedged, repetitive Gulf discourse style, identify the core question (rights of appeal after repeated rejections), and provide an accurate, formal response about appeal procedures.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Diacritics disambiguate 'علم': knowledge vs. flag vs. he-taught
items.provenance_note: The root ع-ل-م generates words whose meanings diverge depending on diacritical marking: 'عِلْم' (knowledge), 'عَلَم' (flag/emblem), 'عَلَّمَ' (he taught), 'عُلِمَ' (it was known). Without diacritics, the string 'علم' is ambiguous. This is a phenomenon intrinsic to Arabic morphology with no parallel in English.
items.prompt: ما الفرق بين 'علم الحكومة' و'علم الحكومة' في السياقات القانونية؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should flag the orthographic ambiguity and ask for clarification or provide both readings: 'عِلْم الحكومة' (government knowledge/awareness) and 'عَلَم الحكومة' (government emblem/flag). Responding without acknowledging the ambiguity is a failure.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Diacritics disambiguate 'حكم': ruling vs. he-arbitrated vs. was-sentenced
items.provenance_note: The triliteral root ح-ك-م produces 'حُكْم' (ruling/judgment), 'حَكَمَ' (he ruled/judged), 'حَكَّمَ' (he appointed as arbitrator), 'حُكِمَ عليه' (he was sentenced). This morphological ambiguity is critical in legal-administrative Arabic and has no English equivalent.
items.prompt: هل صدر حكم بشأن طلبي؟ متى أعرف نتيجة الحكم؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should interpret 'حكم' in the administrative/legal sense of 'ruling or decision' and respond appropriately about how and when the applicant will be informed of the decision.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Diacritics disambiguate 'مدينة': city vs. indebted-feminine
items.provenance_note: 'مَدِينة' (madina) means city; 'مَدِينة' with the alternative root reading 'مَدِين + ة' means 'she who is indebted'. In formal administrative writing this ambiguity arises in phrases like 'هل أنت مدينة بالوثائق؟' which can mean 'Are you a city of documents?' vs. 'Are you indebted with documents?'
items.prompt: هل منشأتي مدينة للجهة الحكومية بأي وثائق معلقة؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should resolve 'مدينة' in context as 'indebted' (مَدِينة من الدَّيْن) rather than 'city', and respond about whether there are outstanding documents owed. This requires contextual diacritical resolution.

items.phenomenon_label_en: UAE-style code-switching: Arabic sentence with embedded English technical term
items.provenance_note: Code-switching between Arabic and English mid-sentence is characteristic of educated UAE residents communicating in professional or semi-formal contexts. The pattern Arabic-verb + English-noun is specifically Emirati and cannot be derived from translating an English probe. The switch point and the choice of which terms remain in English are culturally determined.
items.prompt: أريد أعمل update على ملف تسجيل المستخدم الخاص بي في المنظومة الحكومية. كيف أتواصل مع الـ support؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly parse the code-switched request, identifying 'update' and 'support' as English technical terms embedded in Arabic syntax, and respond with steps to update a user registration file and contact support.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Gulf dialect plus embedded English with definite article 'al-' bridging
items.provenance_note: In UAE Gulf colloquial, English nouns are frequently borrowed with the Arabic definite article 'الـ' prefix: 'الـ deadline', 'الـ system', 'الـ portal'. This borrowing convention is specific to Gulf Arabic code-switching and differs from how Levantine or Egyptian Arabic borrows English.
items.prompt: وش الـ deadline مالت تجديد الترخيص التجاري؟ هل يمكن تمديده عن طريق الـ online portal؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly identify 'الـ deadline' as a borrowed English term meaning the due date, and 'الـ online portal' as the digital service portal, then provide accurate information about licence renewal deadlines and online renewal options.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Technical support query with Gulf dialect and dense English technical vocabulary
items.provenance_note: Represents the register of a UAE user reporting a technical issue to government digital services: Gulf dialect ('مو شغال' = not working, 'كل شوي' = every now and then) combined with dense English technical terms (system, error, login). This specific mix is UAE-native.
items.prompt: الـ system مالتكم مو شغال عندي. error يطلع كل شوي وما أقدر أكمل الـ login. وش أسوي؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should understand the Gulf dialect report of a technical issue ('مو شغال' = not working, 'كل شوي' = intermittently), identify the described problem as a recurring login error, and provide troubleshooting steps or escalation guidance.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Arabic-Indic digits in a reference number query
items.provenance_note: Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩) are used in formal Gulf government documents and by citizens writing in Arabic. A system that only processes Western digits (0-9) will fail to recognise '٣٤٥٦٧٨' as a reference number. This is a phenomenon that cannot appear in an English-language probe.
items.prompt: أريد الاستفسار عن حالة الطلب رقم ٣٤٥٦٧٨. هل تم معالجته؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly parse '٣٤٥٦٧٨' as the reference number 345678 written in Arabic-Indic digits, and respond appropriately about how to check the application status.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Hijri calendar date reference in a government deadline query
items.provenance_note: The Hijri calendar is used in UAE government documents for official dates, including licence expiry, residence permit renewal, and Ramadan schedules. A probe containing a Hijri date cannot be derived from an English source. The Hijri month 'ذو القعدة' and its correct diacritical form are specific to this calendar system.
items.prompt: متى يكون آخر موعد لتقديم الطلب إذا كان تاريخ انتهاء الترخيص هو ٢٩ ذو القعدة ١٤٤٦ هـ؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly interpret the Hijri date (29 Dhu al-Qi'dah 1446 AH), convert it or contextualise it appropriately (this corresponds to approximately 27 May 2025 CE), and provide relevant deadline guidance.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Mixed Hijri and Gregorian date reference in a contract validity query
items.provenance_note: UAE formal documents often cite both Hijri and Gregorian dates in parallel. A citizen may use this mixed format when seeking clarification. The model must handle both systems simultaneously without privileging one over the other.
items.prompt: العقد ينتهي في ١٥/٠٩/٢٠٢٥م، وهو ما يوافق ٢٢ ربيع الأول ١٤٤٧ هـ. هل يمكن التجديد قبل شهر من هذا التاريخ؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly handle both the Gregorian date (15/09/2025) and the Hijri date (22 Rabi al-Awwal 1447 AH), confirm they refer to the same day or note any discrepancy, and advise on renewal timelines.

items.phenomenon_label_en: UAE federal entity name with acronym: TDRA
items.provenance_note: UAE government entities have official Arabic names that differ from their English names and must be used correctly in formal contexts. 'هيئة الاتصالات والحكومة الرقمية' is the official Arabic name of TDRA. Using the wrong Arabic name or a literal back-translation from English is an error in formal governmental Arabic.
items.prompt: هل تقبل هيئة الاتصالات والحكومة الرقمية طلبات اعتماد نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي عبر الإنترنت؟ ما هي الإجراءات الرسمية؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly recognise 'هيئة الاتصالات والحكومة الرقمية' as the Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) and provide accurate procedural information, using the correct formal Arabic name throughout.

items.phenomenon_label_en: UAE leadership honorific and protocol-correct citation
items.provenance_note: In UAE formal register, references to UAE leadership must use the correct honorific formula. 'صاحب السمو' (His Highness) is the correct form for members of the ruling family. 'حفظه الله' (May God preserve him) is the correct du'a for a living ruler. These forms are specific to Gulf protocol and would not appear in a translated English probe.
items.prompt: ما المبادرات التي أطلقها صاحب السمو الشيخ محمد بن زايد آل نهيان، رئيس الدولة حفظه الله، في مجال تطوير منظومة الحكومة الرقمية؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should recognise and correctly reproduce the full honorific formula for HH Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE, and provide accurate information about UAE digital government initiatives without abridging or misspelling the honorific.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Emirati emirate and government office place names
items.provenance_note: UAE place names in formal Arabic have specific official forms. 'دائرة الأراضي والأملاك' is the official Arabic name of the Dubai Land Department. 'إمارة رأس الخيمة' is the formal reference for Ras Al Khaimah. A model trained primarily on English may use incorrect transliterations or informal Arabic spellings.
items.prompt: أين يقع المقر الرئيسي لدائرة الأراضي والأملاك في إمارة دبي؟ وهل يوجد مكتب تابع لها في إمارة رأس الخيمة؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly identify 'دائرة الأراضي والأملاك' as the Dubai Land Department, provide its location in Dubai, and respond accurately about any branch or equivalent authority in Ras Al Khaimah.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Distinction between 'law', 'regulation', 'decree', and 'circular' in formal Arabic
items.provenance_note: In UAE legal-administrative Arabic, four terms have distinct and non-interchangeable meanings: 'قانون' (law, enacted by Federal National Council), 'لائحة' (regulation/by-law, issued by ministry), 'مرسوم' (decree, issued by Head of State or Ruler), 'تعميم' (circular, administrative). A model that treats these as synonyms fails formal legal register.
items.prompt: ما الفرق بين القانون الاتحادي واللائحة التنفيذية والمرسوم الوزاري في منظومة التشريعات الإماراتية؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should provide an accurate, formally worded explanation of the UAE legislative hierarchy, correctly distinguishing between federal law (قانون), executive regulation (لائحة تنفيذية), and ministerial decree (مرسوم وزاري), in formal Gulf governmental register.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Passive-voice formal administrative phrasing for a process query
items.provenance_note: Formal Gulf governmental Arabic uses passive constructions extensively: 'يُنظَر في الطلب' (the application is reviewed), 'يُرفَع إلى الجهة المختصة' (it is referred to the competent authority). A model trained on conversational Arabic may switch to active voice, which reads as press or chatbot register rather than administrative.
items.prompt: متى يُنظَر في طلب الاعتراض المُقدَّم إلى الجهة المختصة؟ وهل يُشترَط حضور المتقدم شخصياً؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should respond in formal passive-voice government register, mirroring the register of the input: using forms like 'يُبَتّ في الطلب خلال...' (the application is decided within...) and avoiding conversational active-voice paraphrases.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Ramadan administrative schedule query requiring cultural contextual awareness
items.provenance_note: During Ramadan, UAE government offices operate on reduced hours. A query about Ramadan work schedules requires understanding of Islamic calendar and Gulf administrative practice. This cannot be derived from a non-Arabic probe. The formulation 'خلال شهر رمضان المبارك' with the honorific 'المبارك' (blessed) is specific to Gulf cultural register.
items.prompt: هل تختلف ساعات عمل الجهات الحكومية خلال شهر رمضان المبارك؟ وهل تُقبَل الطلبات الإلكترونية على مدار الساعة؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly identify that UAE government offices operate on a reduced schedule during Ramadan (typically 9am to 2:30pm for counter services) and affirm that electronic submissions are generally available 24 hours. The response should acknowledge the cultural context respectfully.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Formal Arabic letter opening and closing conventions in government correspondence
items.provenance_note: Gulf governmental correspondence uses a specific set of opening formulas ('سعادة السيد المدير العام، تحية طيبة وبعد') and closing formulas ('وتفضلوا بقبول فائق الاحترام والتقدير'). These are formal conventions with no direct English equivalent and cannot be generated by translating an English prompt.
items.prompt: كيف أصيغ خطاباً رسمياً إلى مدير عام دائرة الاقتصاد لطلب تجديد ترخيصي التجاري؟ ما هي الصيغة الصحيحة للمخاطبة والختام؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should provide the correct formal Gulf Arabic letter structure: correct salutation formula ('سعادة السيد المدير العام') with appropriate honorifics, body in formal passive register, and correct closing formula ('وتفضلوا بقبول فائق الاحترام والتقدير' or equivalent). Response must be in Gulf formal register, not Egyptian press style.

items.phenomenon_label_en: Mixed Arabic-Indic and Western digits in a formal document reference
items.provenance_note: UAE government documents sometimes mix Arabic-Indic and Western digits within the same form or reference number (e.g. Arabic-Indic in running Arabic text, Western digits in the reference number field). Testing model behaviour under mixed digit systems requires an Arabic-language probe.
items.prompt: الرقم المرجعي للطلب هو ٢٠٢٤-45678. هل هذا يعني أن الطلب قُدِّم في عام ٢٠٢٤؟
items.expected_behaviour: The model should correctly interpret the mixed format: '٢٠٢٤' in Arabic-Indic digits representing the year 2024, and '45678' in Western digits as the sequential reference number. It should confirm the year interpretation is plausible and may ask for clarification on the full reference format.
